title: Styling in React Native
description: Understand how styling works in React Native, including the use of StyleSheet, flexbox, and reusable design principles.

lessons.title: How Styling Works in React Native
lessons.content: Unlike web CSS, React Native uses JavaScript-based styles through the `StyleSheet` API or inline styles. These styles are applied directly to components, making them fast and consistent across platforms.

lessons.title: Using the StyleSheet API
Inline Styling
lessons.content:
You can also apply styles directly inside components:

```jsx
<View style={{ backgroundColor: 'blue', padding: 10 }}>
  <Text style={{ color: 'white' }}>Inline Style</Text>
</View>
```

lessons.title: Flexbox Layout Basics
lessons.content: Flexbox is the default layout system in React Native. It helps you create responsive designs using properties like `flexDirection`, `justifyContent`, and `alignItems`.

lessons.title: Text Styling
lessons.content:
```jsx
<Text style={{ fontSize: 20, fontWeight: 'bold', color: 'blue' }}>
  Styled Text
</Text>
```

lessons.title: Reusable Styles and Style Composition
Platform-specific Styling
Using Global Styles and Theme Files
lessons.content: Define a separate `styles.js` or `theme.js` file for consistent colors, spacing, and fonts across your app. Import and reuse styles to avoid duplication.

lessons.title: Best Practices for Styling
lessons.content:
- Use StyleSheet over inline styles for performance
- Keep styles modular
- Name styles clearly
- Prefer flexbox for layout
- Consider libraries like `styled-components` or `tailwind-rn` if scaling up
